messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P0 fired for service inference-eu-embeddings — high 5xx rate and request queue backlog. PD link: https://pd.example/incidents/PD1234. alertwave auto-suppressed 14 duplicate pages (fanout). creating thread to coordinate ownership and mitigation.

alex: Acked. Oncall here. I'll take ownership until 13:00 UTC unless someone closer wants it.

sam: thanks alex. can you confirm customer impact? product monitoring shows elevated latencies and some 429s to a subset of customers.

alex: quick read from logs: region eu-west-1 showing spikes of 5xx from runtime -> kvcache miss/eviction noise. snippet: 
```
error: kv cache eviction rate high
2026-03-15T12:01:02Z inference-runtime: 5xx write_kv_cache
```

liz: infra here. I see a node flapping in pool-gpu-2 — it restarted twice in the last 3m (OOM/killed). correlates with the time of the spike.

mike: +1. autoscaler seems to be thrashing the pool (scale down then scale up). that can amplify KV cache cold start storms.

alex: mitigation plan (start now): 1) pause autoscaler on pool-gpu-2 (liz) 2) increase KV cache TTL on the model-serving pods (sam) 3) reroute new requests to eu-west-2 temporarily (mike) 4) open bridge and PD ticket updates (me).

liz: disabling autoscaler -> done. command: `kubectl annotate deployment inference-pool-gpu-2 scaler.kubernetes.io/paused="true"` :white_check_mark:

sam: bumped KV_TTL on canary to 45m and rolled 2 pods: `kubectl set env cm/inference-config KV_TTL=45m` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serving --selector=pool=pool-gpu-2 --max-unavailable=1`. verification logs look good on canary.

incidentbot: Bridge created: https://meet.example/bridges/INC-PD1234-bridge. Ticket INC-2026-771 opened. customer-impact summary: degraded — ~6-8% of EU embeddings traffic experienced elevated latency/5xx between 12:00-12:20 UTC.

mike: routing change pushed to prefer eu-west-2 for embeddings. canary traffic showing lower latency.

alex: observability note: token-level latency for rerouted traffic dropped from ~950ms to ~420ms. affected customers list compiled; recommend CS notification. who will ping CS?

liz: I'll ping CS ops with a short impact note and ETA. drafting now.

sam: monitoring: error rate trending down but still seeing intermittent bursts ~every 30s. not sustained.

alex: suggested customer message (draft): "We experienced increased inference 5xx and elevated latency between 12:00-12:20 UTC affecting ~6% of embeddings calls in EU. Mitigation actions taken: paused autoscaler on pool-gpu-2 and routed traffic to eu-west-2. Root cause under investigation; we'll follow up with a postmortem." I'll post to #support-status once stable for 30m.

mike: I'll update PD with actions and mark as triaged; assigning to alex.

incidentbot: PD updated: assigned to alex, status: acknowledged -> triaged. next automated ping scheduled in 10m for status update.

alex: follow-up action items captured: - autoscaler threshold tuning and safer cooldown window - investigate node preemption/termination root cause with cloud infra - add gateway backoff/rate-limiter to reduce KV cache storm risk - postmortem owner: sam.

sam: I can own the postmortem. will collect relevant logs, pod lifecycle events, and autoscaler metrics.

liz: operational note: if stable for 30m I'll unpause autoscaler but will change scale-down window to 15m before enabling.

alex: agreed. setting reminder with incidentbot for 10m status check.

mike: also recommending a short runbook edit: add step to reroute to secondary region on elevated eviction spikes. I'll prepare MR.

alex: thanks team. current status: degraded -> improving. PD state: triaged, bridged, owners assigned. will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

end of thread: will reconvene if PD escalates or errors recur.
